title: Micro-tiered retention & probe-driven eviction spec
content:
Context and intent:

This note describes a pragmatic architecture for a micro-tiered KV cache designed to: reduce fragmentation, preserve low tail latency, and provide predictable unit cost across mixed workloads. The approach mixes lightweight probes, transient micro-tiers, and non-blocking compaction to avoid large stop-the-world reclamations.

Key goals:
- Keep per-request critical path short (no IO on hot path).
- Limit memory blowup due to fragmentation to < 8% under typical tenant churn.
- Provide observable signals to automatically tune retention windows and probe rates.
- Graceful backpressure across tenants and shards to preserve SLOs.

High-level design sketch:
1) Micro-tiered retention lanes:
   - Hot lane: extremely short-latency, purely in-memory entries with pinned slot semantics for active prefixes. Kept small per shard (configurable percent of heap).
   - Warm lane: compacted in-memory entries which are eligible for fast probabilistic eviction. These are stored in denser packing and referenced by small indices.
   - Cold lane: sparse entries that may be spilled (optional) to NVMe or compressed store; accessed via async fetch and populate back into warm/hot lanes.

2) Probe-driven admission/eviction:
   - Instead of relying solely on recency counters, we periodically sample entries in the warm lane with a low-rate probe to measure continued usefulness (marginal score).
   - Probe is a no-op read that records whether an item is still hit within probe window. Probe results update a decay score used for eviction ranking.
   - Probe rate is adaptive: increased for tenants/shards with elevated miss tail or higher churn. Metric: kv.eviction.probe_rate_per_shard.

3) Memory layout and allocator model:
   - Use a hybrid lane allocator: small fixed-size blocks for hot lane objects (fast allocate/free), variable-size compact blocks for warm lane (packed tightly by mini-allocator).
   - Warm lane uses a "micropage" unit (e.g., 4KB) and a compact index that maps key -> (micropage_id, offset, length). This minimizes header overhead and reduces fragmentation for variable-length values.
   - Cold lane entries have a lightweight forwarding pointer; compacting them is background-only.

4) Fragmentation scoring and background compaction:
   - Each micropage tracks occupancy histogram (percent used, average free-run length). From that we compute a fragmentation score: frag = free_runs_weighted / occupancy.
   - Background compactor picks high-frag micropages for incremental rewrite. Compaction is cooperative and rate-limited by kv.compactor.tokens_per_second.
   - Compaction operations are done via copy-on-write semantics to avoid invalidating readers: write new micropage, atomically swap index, and enqueue old pages for reclamation once readers drain.

5) Tenant-aware soft quotas and transient lease:
   - Each tenant has a soft quota for warm+hot lanes. When a tenant exceeds soft quota, their admission probability to warm lane drops (probabilistic admission).
   - Tenants may acquire transient leases to pin a small hot-region (for critical workloads). Leases expire and are sampled for continued usage.

6) Eviction policy (combined):
   - Rank candidates by composite score: eviction_score = w_age*age_norm + w_unseen*decay_score + w_frag*fragmentation_locality - w_pref*prefix_priority.
   - Probe updates decay_score; pages with low decay_score are prioritized. Age_norm penalizes very old inactive entries only after they age beyond a threshold.
   - Prefix coalescing: eviction prefers removing whole low-use prefixes when not harmful for cache hit-rate (reduces index churn).

7) Observability and metrics:
   - kv.cache.hit_rate_per_lane (hot/warm/cold)
   - kv.fragmentation.micropage_{p50,p90,p99}
   - kv.eviction.probe_rate_per_shard
   - kv.compaction.cycles_per_minute, kv.compaction.time_per_cycle_ms
   - kv.tenant.soft_quota_violations, kv.tenant.admission_probability
   - Traces: attach span for compaction rewrite and probe evaluation to attribute latency and CPU.

8) Safety and graceful degradation:
   - When fragmentation exceeds threshold, increase compactor throughput and ramp probe admission to aggressively filter cold entries.
   - If compactor cannot keep up, throttle admission globally and enable spill-to-NVMe for the cold lane.

Experimentation plan (short-term):
- Phase A: implement probe sampler + decay score. Run in shadow mode for 2 weeks across 5% of production traffic. Collect hit-rate delta and probe cost.
- Phase B: enable adaptive probe rate with a conservative controller (PID on miss tail). Observe probe CPU and observed hit retention.
- Phase C: implement micropage histograms and a single-threaded compactor. Run mixed workloads to measure fragmentation ratio and compaction overhead.
- Phase D: tenant soft quotas and probabilistic admission; run against spike workloads and measure tenant fairness.

Configuration knobs (exposed):
- kv.lane.hot_percent_per_shard (default 8%)
- kv.probe.base_rate_per_shard (samples/sec)
- kv.probe.max_rate_per_shard
- kv.compactor.max_cycles_per_shard_per_minute
- kv.tenant.soft_quota_margin (percent over commit)
- kv.eviction.weights = "age:0.2,decay:0.6,frag:0.2"

Open questions / risks:
- Probe-induced noise: probes themselves can change the access patterns (self-amplifying). Need to validate that probe reads are accounted as "observer" hits and not promoted incorrectly.
- Copy-on-write compaction cost: worst-case rewrite bandwidth when many micropages fragmented. Need throttling and backoff strategies.
- Spill latency: how to quantify and budget for cold-lane NVMe fetches so we retain tail SLOs.
- Index atomicity: swapping compact index pointers must be safe against concurrent readers (use hazard pointers or epoch reclaim).

Todos (implementation-oriented):
- [ ] Add lightweight probe sampler to warm lane (instrumentation hooks).
- [ ] Implement decay score telemetry and dashboard.
- [ ] Prototype micropage allocator and occupancy histogram.
- [ ] Build single-threaded compactor CLI and safety checks.
- [ ] Draft admission probability controller PR.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight and experimental. Focus review on whether the admission/eviction control loops are sensible and whether observability surfaces capture necessary signals.
- If you have workloads that would benefit from pinned hot region leases, add examples to GH issue linked above.
